label: Weather fact daily
h1: A weather fact every morning, from lightning to hail

items.b: A lightning bolt can heat the air to around 30,000 K, about five times hotter than the Sun's surface (NOAA).
Count the seconds between flash and thunder. Divide by 5 for miles, or by 3 for kilometres.
'When thunder roars, go indoors' is the National Weather Service's rule. If you can hear thunder, you're close enough to be struck.
A tropical storm becomes a hurricane when sustained winds reach 74 mph (119 km/h).
The Atlantic hurricane season officially runs from June 1 to November 30.
To see a rainbow, the Sun has to be behind you and rain in front of you.
The highest wind gust on record not linked to a tornado was 408 km/h, at Barrow Island, Australia, during Cyclone Olivia in 1996 (WMO).
The WMO lists 56.7°C (134°F), Death Valley, 1913, as the hottest air temperature on record. Some researchers dispute it.
The coldest air temperature ever measured was −89.2°C, at Vostok Station, Antarctica, in 1983.
Snowflakes are almost always six-sided because ice crystals form in a hexagonal pattern.
Fog is simply a cloud touching the ground.
When air cools to its dew point, water vapour condenses. That's how dew, fog and clouds form.
Since 2007 the US has rated tornadoes on the Enhanced Fujita scale, from EF0 to EF5, based on damage.
The United States records more tornadoes than any other country, typically more than 1,000 a year.
Jet streams are rivers of fast wind about 9–12 km up, often blowing at over 100 mph.
Thunderstorm clouds (cumulonimbus) can tower more than 12 km into the sky.
The largest US hailstone on record fell in Vivian, South Dakota, in 2010. It was 8 inches across.
El Niño is a warming of the tropical Pacific that shifts rainfall and temperatures around the world.
Because of the Coriolis effect, hurricanes spin counterclockwise in the Northern Hemisphere and clockwise in the Southern.
A hurricane's eye is often calm and clear, and typically 20–40 miles across.
A watch means conditions are right for severe weather. A warning means it's happening or about to. Act on warnings.

Wind chill is how cold it feels on skin when wind strips heat away. The thermometer doesn't change.
Steadily falling air pressure usually means unsettled weather is on the way.
